Aquatic plants , also referred to as hydrophytes , [ 1 ] are vascular plants and non-vascular plants [ 2 ] that have adapted to live in aquatic environments ( saltwater or freshwater ). In lakes , rivers and wetlands , aquatic vegetations provide cover for aquatic animals such as fish , amphibians and aquatic insects , create substrate for benthic invertebrates , produce oxygen via photosynthesis , and serve as food for some herbivorous wildlife. [ 3 ] Familiar examples of aquatic plants include waterlily , lotus , duckweeds , mosquito fern , floating heart , water milfoils , mare's tail , water lettuce , and water hyacinth . [ 4 ]
